verdict.rationale: Honcho documents named-scope API keys bound to one scope for recall (read) and message ingestion (write), and workspaces as isolation containers, which is a first-party but coarse form of access control. Peer scoping in retrieval shapes results rather than enforcing permissions, so it earns no credit. missing for 10: roles or policy/ACL models, fine-grained per-peer/session read-write permissions, audit logging of memory access, detailed docs or independent corroboration of the scoped-key model.
